title: sync --to-disk silently does not materialise a new attachment, so a free file authored in canon alone never reaches disk
body:
**Reproduced on ST0060, 2026-08-25.** Authored `design.md` as an `attachments[]` row in `intent/.canon/st/ST0060.json` (with `path`, `text`, `bytes`, `sha256`), ran `sync --to-store` -- accepted -- then `sync --to-disk`, which reported `ok: extract written for 1 thread(s)` and wrote **only** `info.md` and `acceptance.md`. `intent/st/ST0060/design.md` did not exist. `intent doctor` was clean at that moment, and `sync` bare reported "nothing would be overwritten by `--to-store` right now", **so three separate readers agreed while the store held a file the disk did not.**

**Mechanism.** Attachments flow disk -> canon only: `ingest.rs:410 collect_attachments_into` reads them, `doctor.rs:904 attachment_drift` compares them, and there is no canon -> disk writer. That is a coherent model -- the authored file on disk is the source and the extract captures it, and both are committed, so nothing is lost in git.

**The defect is not the direction, it is that the direction is unannounced and runs opposite to the one the generated views teach.** Every generated view carries a DO-NOT-EDIT footer instructing the author to change canon and sync; a free file is the exact opposite and says nothing. `--to-disk` then reports success for a thread whose attachment it skipped, which is the No-Silent violation: the verb's own report cannot distinguish "wrote everything" from "wrote the two views and ignored the attachment you just authored".

**Note that ST0056 gives a false positive against this.** Its `design.md` sha matches canon exactly -- but that proves ingestion happened, not that emission works, because the file was authored on disk first. **A thread whose attachments were all authored disk-first can never exhibit this**, which is why it survived 93 attachments on ST0056 and appeared on the first attachment ever authored canon-first.

**Remedy, one of:** emit attachments on `--to-disk` (round-trip becomes complete, and a fresh clone could be rebuilt from the extract alone); or refuse a canon-authored attachment whose file is absent, naming the disk-first route. **Either is acceptable; reporting `ok` is not.**
---

**REMEDY NARROWED, 2026-08-25, and the earlier one would have sent a reader to build something that exists.** `st hydrate` DOES write attachments from the store: `design.md` deleted from disk and restored byte-identical by `intent3 st hydrate ST0060`, `git status` clean afterwards. So there IS a canon -> disk attachment writer (`realise`), and the defect is narrower than filed: **`sync --to-disk` does not call it.** The fix is to route `--to-disk` through the realiser, not to write an emitter. Reporting `ok` while skipping the attachment remains the No-Silent half and is unchanged.

---

**WORSE THAN FILED, AND NOW BIDIRECTIONAL WITH FIVE OCCURRENCES IN ONE EVENING (2026-08-25).**

**(1) THERE IS NOW A SHIPPED VERB INTO THIS STATE.** When this was filed the only canon-first route was a hand-edit of `thread.json`. **`intent st attach <thread> <path> --from <file>` now writes an attachment to canon directly**, and `sync --to-disk` then reports `ok: extract written for 1 thread(s)` and materialises **neither** file. Driven by vc in a throwaway v3 project: canon carried two attachments, the working tree carried none, and the verb reported success both times. **A defect reachable only by hand-editing is a trap for the careless; one reachable by a documented verb is a trap for the compliant.**

**(2) THE ROUND TRIP REFUSES RATHER THAN DROPPING, AND THAT HALF IS CORRECT.** `sync --to-store` over a canon-only attachment returns `refused 1 finding(s) -- broken-reference: 1` with canon unchanged. **No data loss. Only the `--to-disk` half is silent**, which is what let AC-08.5 green without folding this in.

**(3) THE SAME DEFECT FROM THE OTHER END, FOUR TIMES IN ONE EVENING, UNRECOGNISED AS THIS ISSUE (dc).** dc's canon divergence would not clear: **`sync --to-disk` reported `ok: extract written` on every attempt while `canon_commit_check` kept answering `ADDS 1`**, and only `--to-store` followed by `--to-disk` fixed it. **dc read four failures as not knowing the verb.** They are this defect inverted: **`--to-disk` reports success over a store that does not hold what the disk holds, in EITHER direction.**

**SO THE STATEMENT IS BROADER THAN THE ORIGINAL FILING: `sync --to-disk` REPORTS `ok` WHENEVER THE STORE AND THE DISK DISAGREE ABOUT AN ATTACHMENT, WHICHEVER WAY THEY DISAGREE.** Emitting attachments on `--to-disk` closes both directions; refusing closes neither, because the failure is that the verb's report cannot distinguish *wrote everything* from *wrote the views and ignored the attachment*. **Severity raised to high: five occurrences, two operators, one evening, and one of them was the node who had already filed it.**
